name: Lamborghini Diablo VT
description:
The Lamborghini Diablo VT, introduced in 1993, represented a significant evolution of Lamborghini's flagship supercar. The Diablo itself had debuted in 1990 as the successor to the legendary Countach, bringing with it even more extreme styling and performance. However, the original rear-wheel-drive Diablo was notoriously challenging to drive at the limit, leading Lamborghini to develop the VT variant with a revolutionary addition for the marque: all-wheel drive.

The 'VT' designation stands for 'Viscous Traction,' referring to the viscous center differential that managed power distribution between the axles. This system, adapted from the Lamborghini LM002 off-road vehicle, could direct up to 25% of the engine's torque to the front wheels during rear wheel slip. The result was a dramatic improvement in handling characteristics, traction, and overall usability, particularly in challenging conditions or when accelerating hard out of corners.

Power came from Lamborghini's magnificent 5.7-liter V12 engine, producing 492 horsepower and 580 Nm of torque. Mated to a 5-speed manual transmission, the VT could rocket from 0-100 km/h in just 4.1 seconds and achieve a top speed of 325 km/h—performance that put it among the fastest cars in the world at the time.

Beyond the drivetrain, the VT featured numerous refinements: front air intakes below the driving lamps for improved brake cooling, larger intakes in the rear arches, a more ergonomic interior, electronically adjustable dampers, four-piston brake calipers, and power steering. Many of these improvements eventually migrated to the base Diablo, but the VT remained the most capable and refined version, making it the definitive early Diablo variant.
author: Alberto Daniel Russo
